channel.title: Diffbrief · Inference
channel.description: Daily inference stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: vLLM tuning reaches 101 tok/s on one GB10 for Inkling 2 Mini
item.description: The tuned setup reports 101 tok/s for one request, 195.7 tok/s across four concurrent requests, and a 9.7-second first token for a 32K prompt. These measurements offer concrete performance targets for engineers tuning local inference.

item.title: A public dashboard tracks llama.cpp inference on AMD Ryzen and Radeon
item.description: The dashboard compares prompt processing and text generation across llama.cpp builds, models, quantizations, and AMD hardware; its benchmark workflow and results are public. Engineers can use it to inspect local-inference performance and how the measurements were produced.

item.title: ShowNow cuts world-model input latency from 620 to 208 ms
item.description: ShowNow prepares up to eight action-conditioned futures during playback; on one H100, its 5B model generates 480p video at 16 fps and cuts median input-to-display latency to 208 ms. The speculative approach shows how compute during playback can reduce interactive model latency.

item.title: An AMD llama.cpp fork reports faster generation and prefill on Radeon GPUs
item.description: The author reports generation rising from 35 to 55 tokens per second and prefill from 700 to 1,300 tokens per second with an AMD-focused fork, while noting results may vary. The measurements make this worth investigating for teams serving local models on AMD GPUs.

item.title: DeepSeek traffic on Novita and StreamLake routes appears to pass through ByteDance Ark
item.description: The investigation traces selected DeepSeek routes to ByteDance Ark and reports weekly token volumes, while raising questions about Novita’s zero-data-retention status and provider chain. Inference teams should scrutinize routing and subprocessors when evaluating privacy claims.

item.title: llama.cpp v1.1.0 adds per-tensor quantization targets and refactors server scheduling
item.description: The release adds quantization by bit-per-weight or size budget, separates DFlash draft methods, refactors llama-server slot scheduling and deprecates the old batch API. These changes matter to teams running local models and maintaining integrations.

item.title: Register recycling cuts NVFP4 attention latency by up to 1.64× on Blackwell
item.description: The kernel splits score tiles into reusable register slots, reducing Tensor Core idle time; latency improves up to 1.64×, with end-to-end inference reductions up to 15.34% across four workloads. Its integration into FlashInfer makes the measured optimization relevant to serving engineers.

item.title: Qwen3-0.6B runs bare-metal in a 24 KB assembly kernel
item.description: The project runs Qwen3-0.6B without an operating system, reports token-exact parity across 1–32 vCPUs, and measures up to 136.6 tokens per second in QEMU KVM. Its concrete implementation and performance figures make it a useful study in minimal model inference.

item.title: Inkling 2 Mini uses a looped MoE and mixed-precision weights for local inference
item.description: Inkling 2 Mini has 26B total parameters, 3B active per token, and a looped MoE whose middle 12 layers run three times; its checkpoint mixes NVFP4 and MXFP8. Those design choices offer useful context for serving the model on a single RTX PRO 6000.

item.title: vLLM meetup highlights prefill optimization and agent-written kernels
item.description: The meetup covered high-throughput prefill, pipeline-parallelism optimization, agent-written kernels, multimodal models, and support for upcoming NVIDIA hardware. These are practical directions for engineers working on inference throughput and kernel development.

item.title: CodecOPSD prunes 66% of video-conditioning tokens for 2× faster denoising
item.description: Codec-based pruning removes 66% of condition tokens on average with almost no quality drop, making denoising 2× faster and shrinking KV-cache memory by up to 73%. The method targets conditioning overhead that can dominate visual generation costs.

item.title: VenusOCR2.0 reaches 96.45 on OmniDocBench with parallel draft decoding
item.description: A 1B recognizer pairs dynamic-resolution vision encoding and compact table tokens with a 67M parallel draft module; it scores 96.45 overall and 98.57 on formula CDM. Its decoding and tokenization choices matter to teams balancing document accuracy and throughput.

item.title: ExecuTorch-TensorRT runs a 3.6B robot policy on an 8 GB Jetson
item.description: The pipeline compiles PyTorch models with TensorRT into ExecuTorch programs, running within 4% of the fastest measured TensorRT setup; a 3.6B policy fits on an 8 GB Jetson Orin Nano. This offers a practical path to deploying large robot policies without shipping PyTorch.

item.title: Cosmos 3 Nano runs on GPUs with 12 GB of VRAM through CPU offloading
item.description: The Cosmos-Framework package offloads model weights to system RAM, and an FP8 checkpoint reduces peak GPU memory; the post benchmarks several RTX cards and modalities. These techniques and measurements help engineers assess memory-latency tradeoffs for local model inference.

item.title: AWS Lambda inference splits Qwen layers across functions, with an 80x loss
item.description: The 9.3 GB model is split across Lambda jobs, one per layer and token block, to fit a 3 GB limit. The experiment probes whether CPU-based, highly parallel serverless execution can make model inference practical.

item.title: NariQ quantizes Qwen3.8-27B to 3 bits with near-BF16 task scores
item.description: The 3-bit quantization matches or exceeds BF16 on several reported agentic, math, and multimodal benchmarks, with decode speeds described as comparable to other quants. The results suggest a much smaller model file may retain useful quality, though running it currently requires a llama.cpp fork.

item.title: GB200 delivers more scientific output per joule than H100 in tested workloads
item.description: Across four LAMMPS simulations, GB200 NVL72 delivered 9–17% more atom-timesteps per joule; ICON delivered about 20% more simulated days per joule with 40% fewer GPUs. System-level power measurements show why GPU-only metrics can understate efficiency.

item.title: SpecWM refines draft world-model video and reaches 1.63× speedup
item.description: SpecWM checks draft chunks against a target model’s latent velocity field and can accept, refine or reject them; on WBench Navigation it reports 1.63× speedup and raises NavScore from 75.99 to 85.63. Reusing verification to correct drafts offers a practical alternative to regenerating rejected output.

item.title: Posterior matching distillation targets broader teacher coverage with any-step sampling
item.description: PMD matches exponentially tilted posterior means, and its stochastic student supports different sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without retraining. The approach targets a diversity limitation of reverse-KL distillation for image and video generation.

item.title: A beginner’s guide sets up local AI with Inkling, Qwen and Unsloth
item.description: The guide aims to set up a private, home-hosted ChatGPT alternative on Windows using Inkling, Qwen or Unsloth. It could help engineers evaluate a simple local-model setup, though the excerpt gives no performance or hardware details.

item.title: MemOnce compresses LLM memory and reconstructs KV caches on demand
item.description: MemOnce stores selected final-layer hidden states as compact memories, then retrieves them and decodes KV caches for attention, targeting linear-time growth and lower GPU memory use. The design addresses a key cost of long-running LLM interactions.

item.title: Open-weight models can be used privately without high-end hardware
item.description: The guide argues that users can run open-weight models privately without expensive GPU hardware or specialist knowledge. That offers engineers another path for handling sensitive data and choosing how models are deployed.

item.title: Accenture sequences six levers to reduce Bedrock token spend
item.description: The guide describes six composable optimization levers, a recommended sequence and their use across four client engagements as token spend grows despite falling per-token prices. The cost-control approach is directly relevant to scaling model workloads, though the excerpt omits the specific levers and savings.

item.title: SageMaker Inference review covers 13 launches for capacity and GPU fit
item.description: The roundup covers 13 launches, including fitting more models on each GPU, serving models too large for one instance, cross-Region routing and post-launch tuning. These are directly relevant serving capabilities, though the excerpt gives no performance or cost results.

item.title: SageMaker routes inference across Regions when local capacity falls short
item.description: A single invocation path can span endpoints and inference components across Regions and accounts, preferring the local Region and shifting new requests when it cannot serve reliably. This offers a concrete resilience option for inference deployments, though the excerpt gives no failover measurements.

item.title: Post-training quantization fits Qwen3.5-4B in 1.23 GB with 330 exact-answer solves
item.description: The method combines trellis-code quantization, Fisher-information-based bit allocation and distillation; a 1.23 GB Qwen3.5-4B model solves 330 of 540 exact-answer problems. The recipe, code and GPU cost are provided, giving serving engineers a testable route to smaller models.

item.title: NarrowSpec speeds speculative decoding with smaller draft widths
item.description: Halving or quartering draft width preserves acceptance and yields 1.06–1.44× end-to-end speedups in tested single-request setups, with gains also reported at larger batches. The technique targets draft-model compute without requiring a matching-width residual stream.

item.title: OpenRouter removes providers and 125 endpoints from ZDR eligibility
item.description: OpenRouter says it off-boarded three providers and removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility after researchers reported data-policy failures at inference providers. Teams routing prompts through intermediaries should verify which providers and endpoints handle their data.

item.title: OpenRouter says some MiniMax prompts may have been accessed later
item.description: OpenRouter says unique test URLs in MiniMax prompts were accessed 40–130 hours later, including requests routed through other providers; it reports that the issue appears to involve MiniMax and forwarding providers. Teams sending sensitive prompts through inference intermediaries should check provider data handling.

item.title: Inference engineering covers the trade-offs of APIs, GPU fleets and KV caches
item.description: The deep dive compares frontier-model APIs, inference providers and self-operated GPU fleets, citing examples of companies cutting per-token costs by moving to open models. It addresses practical choices around cost, operations and serving capacity.

item.title: Distributed KV caching can cut self-hosted LLM cost and time to first token
item.description: The post says distributed KV caching with ElastiCache can reduce inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%, and shows an agent skill that evaluates and configures it. The figures make this a useful lead for teams repeating context across turns.

item.title: HyperPod Global Inference Gateway routes requests across clusters and Regions
item.description: The managed gateway offers one endpoint, selects a cluster, fails over automatically, and uses SigV4 and IAM over PrivateLink. It is relevant to teams weighing cross-cluster inference routing and authentication, though the excerpt gives no performance results.

item.title: SageMaker monitors inference endpoints for latency drift and idle GPUs
item.description: SageMaker tracks latency, GPU utilization, and serving configuration, then surfaces findings with a path to benchmark alternatives before applying changes. This adds operational signals for teams tuning inference cost and performance.

item.title: LightningMoBA speeds sparse attention with dynamic routing and KV reuse
item.description: Dynamic routing, KV-centric task ownership and runtime pipelining deliver 1.20–1.60× faster end-to-end generation at matched Top-16 retention, while raising mean RULER score from 74.42 to 75.28. The co-design of sparse selection and GPU execution offers a measurable path to faster long-context inference.

item.title: Coding agents help a developer get an LLM running on an FPGA
item.description: The author recounts using coding agents to program an FPGA to run an LLM, including the surprises encountered while working in an unfamiliar hardware domain. It offers a concrete look at how agents can broaden the range of systems engineers can prototype, though no performance results are given.

item.title: FlashMorph2 selects hybrid-attention layers on-policy
item.description: FlashMorph2 evaluates discrete hybrid architectures end to end and jointly adapts layer scores and model weights; it improves RULER by 2.42 points over FlashMorph with selection taking 0.72–3.57 GPU hours. This is a measured approach to trading attention-model quality against efficiency.

item.title: VSpark speeds up vision-language-action decoding 1.28× to 2.10× without loss
item.description: VSpark combines calibrated action-noise rollouts, hidden-feature alignment and reuse of predictions from rejected drafts; across four VLAs it achieves 1.28×–2.10× speedups while preserving lossless decoding. These techniques address speculative decoding’s poor acceptance when distinct tokens encode similar robot motions.

item.title: Dynamo uses cache-aware routing and delta transfers to speed RL rollouts
item.description: Dynamo coordinates distributed RL rollouts with KV-aware routing, compressed weight-delta transfers and worker recovery; it also integrates with several RL stacks. These serving patterns address wasted prompt computation and rollout delays in training systems.

item.title: A 4.5M-parameter TTS model claims 70× real-time CPU inference
item.description: The model is described as running text-to-speech at 70× real time on CPU and costing $10 to train; ONNX and GGUF are listed. Small local speech models could change the economics of voice features.

item.title: WebRTC's late-packet dropping can disrupt voice AI under packet loss
item.description: The piece argues that WebRTC drops late audio packets to preserve real-time latency, which can leave voice AI missing speech when packets are lost. The latency-versus-audio-completeness tradeoff matters when choosing transports for voice systems.

item.title: DWD removes latent decoders and cuts Wan video warping error by 23%
item.description: DWD adds a final-step pixel prediction head to latent generators, removing the decoder while preserving the denoising trajectory; on Wan video it reduces warping error by 23%. The method targets both inference cost and visible video artifacts.

item.title: CriticNPU uses hardware bottleneck estimates to guide inference-chip search
item.description: CriticNPU filters weak NPU designs before simulation and uses operator runtimes to identify prefill and decode bottlenecks, with a Roofline-style model calibrated from observations. This could make expensive LLM-inference architecture searches more sample-efficient.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon reaches 127 tokens per second, versus 46 for Carbon
item.description: The author models leaderboard results and reports that Gemini 4 Neon was served at 127 tokens per second versus 46 for Carbon, then projects Neon’s performance against Opus 5.5. The analysis highlights how serving speed can affect user-facing model comparisons, though the headline matchup is a projection.

item.title: TIDEWAY unifies GPU and host memory for local MoE inference
item.description: TIDEWAY treats GPU VRAM and host RAM as one pool, pairing phase-aware layouts with CUDA Graph execution under expert paging. The design targets memory-tier thrashing when serving large MoE models on consumer devices.

item.title: FastFrames cuts video-generation latency with lighter decoding and cache updates
item.description: FastFrames reports that VAE decoding and KV-cache updates account for over half of end-to-end latency, then replaces them with lighter alternatives; its 1.3B model runs at 36 ms per frame on one B200. The profiling and measured changes offer actionable lessons for latency-sensitive inference pipelines.

item.title: Cerebras splits inference prefill onto GPUs and decode onto wafer-scale systems
item.description: Cerebras says its production setup uses GPUs for prompt prefill and its wafer-scale systems for output decode, delivering five times more tokens per megawatt at the same speed. The design and efficiency claim are directly relevant to serving capacity and hardware trade-offs.

item.title: Tamserve tracks live video with SAM 3 and a lightweight between-frame tracker
item.description: Tamserve runs SAM 3 every few frames and uses EdgeTAM between them; on an RTX 4090 it reports 16-camera people tracking, 14× less GPU per frame, and flat 3.5 GB memory on a 3,000-frame video. The measurements show a concrete design for scaling video inference beyond a single tracked clip.

item.title: Sparse attention shifts long-context scoring into a tuned indexer
item.description: The indexer uses batched matmul and a fused epilogue; choosing one key head avoids decode-time growth, while fusing Top-k cuts logit writes. These co-design details offer practical levers for improving long-context inference throughput.

item.title: Decision models can gate LLM calls with typed answers and explicit probabilities
item.description: PostHog describes production uses for decision models, which return typed answers with probabilities and can be up to 444.6 times cheaper and 193.6 times faster than frontier models. Using them to gate LLM calls can reduce cost and latency on simpler tasks.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes much longer than rivals on a private eval
item.description: On a private eval, Gemini 4 Carbon reportedly took close to an hour on tasks that Opus and Astra completed in minutes; one listed Carbon run took 22 minutes. Real-world latency and cost can matter as much as model capability when choosing a serving API.

item.title: TrnRT serves GLM-5.3 Flash on AWS Trainium with a cache-aware router
item.description: The open-source engine reports serving two GLM-5.3 Flash instances on one eight-chip Trn2 box and 3.57 million tokens per minute on AgentX benchmarks. Its fused NKI decode kernels and cost comparison make it relevant to teams evaluating non-Nvidia inference hardware.

item.title: MovieRoll compresses video-generation KV cache by up to 78%
item.description: MovieRoll combines streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation and hierarchical KV-cache compression; the cache method reduces memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. The work addresses a concrete memory bottleneck in long-horizon generative inference.

item.title: Vera Rubin reports 5–10× higher agentic-inference throughput per watt than GB300
item.description: Provisional MLPerf Endpoints results report 5×–10× higher throughput per watt and 3×–5× greater interactivity at matched concurrency, with prefix caching, state reuse and routing among the techniques cited. Serving teams can use the results to assess how hardware and workload-aware optimizations affect agent inference.

item.title: Hugging Face routes Inference Providers through OpenRouter for live provider selection
item.description: Hugging Face now sends language-model requests through OpenRouter, which selects among providers using live price, speed, and reliability measurements and retries after failures. This offers a practical look at multi-provider inference routing with an unchanged client API.

item.title: Test-time Baking speeds view synthesis rendering by up to 23×
item.description: TTB bakes cross-view attention mappings into a lightweight MLP and separates context inputs from targets to avoid a modality mismatch, reporting rendering speedups up to 23×. The method illustrates how cached or distilled computation can accelerate learned rendering without giving up as much quality.

item.title: MMFlash speeds speculative decoding for vision-language models by up to 3.58×
item.description: MMFlash adaptively prioritizes visually dependent tokens and uses sparse attention for long video inputs, reporting lossless speedups up to 3.58×. The results target the acceptance-rate and attention costs that shape multimodal serving latency.

item.title: RealtimeVAD reports 100 ms earlier speech-end detection on assistant logs
item.description: An adaptive 10 ms energy detector reportedly detected speech end about 110 ms earlier across roughly 3,200 turns, later settling at 100 ms after a fix for quiet speech; it trades extra false positives for speed. The approach may help voice-assistant pipelines start speculative generation sooner.

item.title: Bedrock attributes AI inference costs to the IAM identity behind each call
item.description: Bedrock propagates IAM identity and organizational tags from inference calls into CUR 2.0 and Cost Explorer without tool-specific instrumentation. This gives AI platform teams a way to track per-user and per-team spend across coding and productivity tools.

item.title: Adaptive decoding escalates uncertain Qwen3-0.6B steps from 4-bit to 8-bit
item.description: On replayed GSM8K steps, an entropy gate ranked argmax flips with AUC 0.93; in live problems its 16% escalation rate used 0.87 of all-high weight bytes, but scores did not significantly separate from either precision baseline. The method is promising, but its live benefit remains uncertain.
